labels.label: bzprop:c3s3p6_dual_sous_variete

hypotheses.paper: L a linear subvariety of dimension p of S(n), -1 <= p <= n
hypotheses.note: L = linearSubvariety M; p = dimS L, an integer, dim M - 1; the range is dimS_mem_Icc

questions: « dimension » of a linear subvariety s(L - {O}) is read dim L - 1, with ∅ of dimension -1 (the proof l.763-764: « F(L) ∪ {O} … de dimension (p+1) »); checked at ∅, S(n) and a point (prop7_empty_univ, prop7_point).

labels.label: bzprop:c3s3p7_noyau_support

hypotheses.note: carried for D(noyau W) = support D(W) and ν(W)+σ(DW) = n-1; D(support W) = noyau D(W) and σ(W)+ν(DW) = n-1 hold for every part W

findings: l.772-773 « D transforme le noyau (resp. support) de W dans le support (resp. noyau) de D(W) » holds with equality: D(noyau W) = support D(W) and D(support W) = noyau D(W). The first needs W closed (for an open hemisphere W, D(noyau W) = D(∅) = S(n) while D(W) is a point; argued, not formalized); the paper assumes W ∈ C(S(n)).
questions: « transforme … dans » read as « onto » (equality), the stronger of into/onto; both are proved.

labels.label: bzprop:c3s3p8_dual_corps_convexe
findings: l.784 prints « est un convexe » ([sic?], OQ-160 (a)); the printed form holds for the dual of any part (claim (a)), so it is weaker than the proof gives. prop8 proves both: D(K) is a closed convex part, and D(K) is a corps convexe (isCorpsConvexeS_D), so either ruling of OQ-160 (a) marks with no Lean change. The interior of D(K) is obtained from σ(D K) = n (Prop. 7) via Convex.interior_nonempty_iff_affineSpan_eq_top; the printed proof's « σ(W) = n; ν(W) = -1 » characterization is used in that direction only.
questions: OQ-160 (a): printed « convexe » vs « corps convexe » — not resolved here; both proved by the one declaration prop8.

labels.label: bzrem:c3s3r1_transposition

hypotheses.paper: ℝⁿ, GL(n,ℝ), GS(n-1,ℝ), S(n-1), W ∈ C(S(n-1))
hypotheses.note: index shifted: ℝⁿ⁺¹, GLR (n+1), GSR n, S n, every n ≥ 0 (the paper's n ≥ 1); D_smul (D(hW) = ᵗh⁻¹ D(W)) for every part

findings: l.864-866 « la représentation duale de GL(n,R) est un automorphisme de GL(n,R) : la transposition » is imprecise: the dual representation for the dot product is g ↦ ᵗg⁻¹ (dotPairing_dualRep: ⟨g x, ᵗg⁻¹ y⟩ = ⟨x, y⟩), an automorphism (dualRepEquiv); the transposition g ↦ ᵗg reverses products (an anti-automorphism of GL(m) for m ≥ 2), and with Δ(g) = ᵗg the formula of l.870 fails: g = diag(2,1), W = {s(1,1)} in S(1) gives ᵗg W = {s(2,1)} ≠ {s(1/2,1)} = D(g(D W)) (transpose_literal_differs). With Δ induced by g ↦ ᵗg⁻¹, every printed assertion is proved: Δ is an involutive automorphism of GS(n,ℝ) and Δ(g) W = D(g(D W)) for every W ∈ C(S(n)) (remark_transposition).
questions: « la transposition » read as the dual (contragredient) representation g ↦ ᵗg⁻¹, which the same sentence names; the literal transposition g ↦ ᵗg is refuted for the formula. Which is the statement of record? Under the ᵗg⁻¹ reading the row could be marked.

instances: Benzecri.Sphere.prop7_empty_univ: σ(∅) = -1, D(∅) = S(n), ν(S(n)) = n; σ(S(n)) = n, D(S(n)) = ∅, ν(∅) = -1; and Prop. 7's σ + ν(D) = n - 1 at both, as a Lean term from prop7
Benzecri.Sphere.prop7_point: for a point x of S(n), σ({x}) = 0, ν({x}) = -1, D({x}) a closed hemisphere, ν(D{x}) = n - 1, σ(D{x}) = n
Benzecri.Sphere.transpose_literal_differs: g = diag(2,1) on ℝ², W = {s(1,1)}: the literal transposition fails the Remark's formula
kb_proposals: Dimensions of linear subvarieties of S(E): Benzecri.Sphere.dimS A = finrank (span F A) - 1 : ℤ (∅ ↦ -1, s(L-O) ↦ dim L - 1); σ = dimS ∘ supportK, ν = dimS ∘ noyau (Chapter3/DualiteSn).

On S(n), L^⊥ for dotPairing: finrank_add_finrank_orth (via linearEquivOfInjective + Subspace.finrank_add_finrank_dualAnnihilator_eq) and orth_orth; D(D(lin L)) = lin L without closedness (D_D_linearSubvariety).

Transpose for the dot product without matrices in proofs: transp f := toLin' (toMatrix' f)ᵀ and transp_eq_of (characterization by ⟨f x, y⟩ = ⟨x, f' y⟩ through dotPairing_injective) gives comp/id/involution in one line each; GL(n+1)-equivariance D(h • W) = ᵗh⁻¹ • D(W) is D_smul.
dotPairing_comm already exists in scaffold Chapter3/ConeAppuiAlpha (same namespace): DualiteSn uses dotPairing_swap to avoid the clash; merge at graduation.

Interior of a cone-defined part: interior of a pos cone is a pos cone via interior_smul₀; then isOpen_ofCone; a nonzero interior point via dense_compl_singleton.inter_open_nonempty (isCorpsConvexeS_D).
